chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who struck another man on the head, causing his tongue to become heavy (impaired speech), he is presented with all the letters of the alphabet. Then, he is given the blood money (diyah) proportional to the letters he could not pronounce clearly from among them.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or compensation for injury/death
key_terms.حُرُوفُ الْمُعْجَمِ: The letters of the alphabet (specifically Arabic)

ai.seo_question: How is blood money calculated for speech impairment caused by a head injury in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential method for assessing 'diyah' (blood money) for speech impairment, specifically linking the compensation to the loss of articulation of the Arabic alphabet's letters. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of quantifying bodily damages based on functional loss, where the victim is tested against the 'huruf al-mu'jammah' (alphabetical letters) to determine the precise proportion of the full compensation owed for the specific letters he can no longer pronounce clearly.
